topic: How an early announcement opened the Berlin Wall's checkpoints

sentences.text: In 1989, one press-conference answer opened the Berlin Wall.
To see how, start with a note.
sentences.editorial: turn to context, not a factual claim

sentences.text: Spokesman Günter Schabowski has just been handed it.
Asked when it starts, he says: immediately, without delay.
West German news tells viewers the borders are open.
That night, guards at Bornholmer Straße let people through.
A wall that stood for decades opened on one unprepared answer.

claims.claim: A Politburo press conference on 9 November 1989 prematurely announced that East Germans could travel without restrictions.
claims.excerpt: occurred after a Politburo press conference on 9 November 1989 prematurely announced that East Germans could travel without restrictions

claims.claim: The press conference was led by Günter Schabowski, began at 18:00 CET on 9 November, and was broadcast live on East German television and radio.
claims.excerpt: led by Günter Schabowski, the outgoing party leader in East Berlin and top party spokesman as Secretary for Information, beginning at 18:00 CET on 9 November and broadcast live on East German television and radio

claims.claim: Shortly before the press conference Schabowski was handed a note announcing the changes, but given no further instructions on how to handle the information.
claims.excerpt: Shortly before the press conference, he was handed a note from Krenz announcing the changes, but given no further instructions on how to handle the information.
claims.context: He had not been involved in the discussions about the new regulations and had not been fully updated.

claims.claim: Asked when the regulations would take effect, Schabowski replied that, as far as he knew, it takes effect immediately, without delay.
claims.excerpt: Schabowski replied, "As far as I know, it takes effect immediately, without delay"
claims.context: Wikipedia gives this as an English rendering of the German; it calls his answer an apparent assumption based on the note's opening paragraph.

claims.claim: West German news told viewers that East Germany's borders were open: the dpa bulletin at 19:04 said citizens could cross the inner German border "immediately", and ARD's Tagesthemen said the borders were open to everyone.
claims.excerpt: The West German Deutsche Presse-Agentur issued a bulletin at 19:04 which reported that East German citizens would be able to cross the inner German border "immediately".
claims.context: Tagesthemen anchor Hanns Joachim Friedrichs: the GDR announced that, starting immediately, its borders are open to everyone.

claims.claim: At 22:45 (alternatively given as 23:30) on 9 November, Harald Jäger, commander of the Bornholmer Straße crossing, yielded and let guards open the checkpoints.
claims.excerpt: at 22:45 (alternatively given as 23:30) on 9 November, Harald Jäger, commander of the Bornholmer Straße border crossing, yielded, allowing guards to open the checkpoints
